A.proof: Common positive submeasure; independent branch-revealed MI finite via KL chain rule; exceptional components cost mP/delta; single h2 difference.

B.correction: The modulus is not globally monotone in delta. Choose a nonmaximal common submeasure of mass1-delta when classical TV<=quantum trace distance delta.
B.new_functional: R_marg(E): regularized Holevo supremum with every average one-mode marginal Gaussian; distinct from old R_G.

C.statement: At fixed E and a fixed finite deterministic Gaussian displacement schedule, independent equiprobable-message random coherent product codebooks with M_m>=exp(Rm),R>0 have max_i trace distance to their empirical moment-matched Gaussian marginal tending to0 almost surely.
C.cost: Strict fixed slack gives eventual feasibility almost surely. At design cost<=1, common random rescaling gives exact feasibility and preserves convergence; its average whole-block trace perturbation is o(1).
C.operational_consequence: Any reliable code sequence with d_m->0 has limsup log(M_m)/m<=H_G(1)+c0/E by Holevo-Fano. This applies to the defined typical books when feasible.

refuted_auxiliary_inferences.inference: Trace-close to a prescribed Gaussian and bounded energy imply trace-close to the moment-matched Gaussian.
refuted_auxiliary_inferences.counterexample: rho_L=(1-1/L)|0><0|+(1/L)|L><L|, energy1, D(rho_L,vacuum)=1/L but sigma_L=gamma_1 and D(rho_L,sigma_L)->1/2.

refuted_auxiliary_inferences.inference: A Gaussian design saturating the cost in expectation produces feasible unadjusted books with probability tending to1.
refuted_auxiliary_inferences.counterexample: For iid CN(0,1), empirical mean cost<=1 with probability tending to1/2 by the CLT for a sum of exponentials.
refuted_auxiliary_inferences.repair: Strict design slack or the explicitly analysed common rescaling.

limitations: C requires E and a finite Gaussian schedule fixed before the block limit.
Uniform message distribution; no arbitrary postselection or message-bearing covariance schedule.
No uniform high-energy blocklength or interchange of E and block limits.
No claim of full-block Gaussian approximation.
No equality of R_marg with an operational constrained-code capacity.
No proof that any given random book has a reliable decoder.
No unrestricted Gaussian-protocol converse or novelty certificate.
